liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (6 reviews): Reviewer says this version climbs to very fuzzy heights, returns, and climbs again; worth getting for it alone; Described as a long-lost, great version, already showing the jazzy, progressive 1970s style [10][11][12][13][14][17]
- **Caution (Do Not Stop on Tracks)** (3 reviews): Caution comes straight out of the Sugar Magnolia ending, with Phil especially strong; Caution is described as a driving, chugging monster that steamrolls the listener [12][14][17]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): Reviewer calls it a hot opener [21]
- **Black Throated Wind** (1 review): Reviewer recommends this as a good early version of the song [16]
- **Next Time You See Me** (1 review): Slow-grinding blues version with a great harmonica solo; the audience tape renders it better than the soundboard [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-04-29.mtx.sirmick.98401.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 185 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1972-04-29.sbd.cousinit.18523.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 177 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: This soundboard mix has Phil prominent throughout and differs from the earlier seed; Keith briefly loud in Playin' [2]
- **gd72-04-29.aud.vernon.5250.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 185 min; rated 4.52/5 by 23 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is imperfect, but clearer than the degraded soundboard on Next Time You See Me; Audience recording is clear and clean, with little audience noise during the songs; Best audience tape the reviewer has heard: balanced, with some crowd and distance, and no clapping into the mic [16][18][20]
- **gd72-04-29.sbd.vernon.17026.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 172 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [4]. Said about its sound: Rated about B-: the soundboard tape is degraded and subdued, though the audience patches bother less; EQ helps; Sound is poor for a soundboard, but still worth hearing [11][13]
- **gd1972-04-29.sbd.sirmick.32877.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 172 min [5]. Said about its sound: Volume adjusted, low and mid frequencies boosted, highs reduced, and hiss reduction applied [5]
- **gd72-04-29.matrix.vernon.17025.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 4 songs; 59 min; rated 4.86/5 by 7 [9]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the matrix well done; Matrix sound quality is rated very good [10][17]

## Around the show

- German crowd reacts mostly at the starts and ends of songs, apparently not following the lyrics [18]
- Reviewer had waited for this show to circulate as a companion to the 4/26 show [11]
- Reviewer says this Dark Star is overlooked next to other tour versions such as 4/24 and 5/11 [13]
- Reviewer finds the show good but not above average for the tour [20]
- Uploader says the prominent bass recalls the 8/4/76 recording and suggests a possible monitor soundboard source [2]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-04-29.mtx.sirmick.98401.flac16**: source: Soundboard/Audience Matrix by Sir Mick [1]. Also: Matrix blending soundboard and audience sources; short soundboard openings patched from audience on Playin' and Greatest Story Ever Told; Casey Jones had a soundboard flaw, so audience was patched in; crowd and tuning gaps filled from audience; Both sources were originally put into circulation by Matt Vernon and the tapers [1]
- **gd1972-04-29.sbd.cousinit.18523.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Cousinit; source: SBD > Master Reel [2]. Also: Audience patch source believed to be a Uher reel machine at 4.75 cm/sec, then cassette to CD-R [2]
- **gd72-04-29.aud.vernon.5250.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience [3]. Also: Audience master possibly Uher reel machine at 4.75 cm/sec, via reels and cassette, converted to SHN by Matt Vernon; Transfer was made from eurodead.net seed disks using EAC [3]
- **gd72-04-29.sbd.vernon.17026.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Matt Vernon; source: Soundboard with audience patches [4]
- **gd1972-04-29.sbd.sirmick.32877.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by SirMick; source: remaster of shnid 17026 [5]. Also: Remaster of shnid 17026: about forty small dropouts repaired and large pops removed [5]
- **gd72-04-29.matrix.vernon.17025.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Matt Vernon; source: Soundboard/Audience Matrix [9]

## Art and photos

- Photo by Caine Schneider (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 4/29/72 Musikhalle, Hamburg, West Germany](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26860491695/) [23]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26860491695/) [24]
